news.title: UEFA declare loss of confidence in Infantino after World Cup sell-off controversy
news.lede: This content is provided by Exco Player and may use cookies or similar technologies. Please click 'Allow and Continue' below to load the content. FIFA president Gianni Infantino has “lost the confidence” of UEFA over a plan to sell stakes in a World Cup company to private investors, the European football governing body has said. Infantino announced overnight that the plan would not proceed after three confederations rejected it, with UEFA going further and saying it would boycott FIFA competitions until the proposal was scrapped.

news.title: Infantino under pressure as Uefa demands accountability over failed World Cup plan
news.lede: Uefa has declared it has no confidence in Fifa President Gianni Infantino after he abandoned a controversial plan to sell a stake in World Cup profits to private investors, deepening a leadership crisis in world football. The proposal sought to place Fifa's commercial operations, including the men's and women's World Cups, into a $20 billion company with 20% owned by private investors. The plan collapsed yesterday (2 August) following strong opposition from Uefa, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), CONCACAF and an internal revolt within Fifa. Aleksander Čeferin, Uefa President, said the current Fifa leadership had lost the confidence of Europe and many others in global football, insisting those responsible for the proposal must be held accountable.

news.title: Pressure on Gianni Infantino increases as Uefa members prepare to oppose re-election
news.lede: European nations to withdraw letters of support for Fifa president. Appetite to ensure Infantino is quickly removed from post. European countries are planning to increase the pressure on Gianni Infantino with a mass withdrawal of letters supporting his re-election as Fifa president. Infantino’s reign is in severe peril after the collapse of his privately backed scheme to sell off chunks of the World Cup, which was largely scuppered when Uefa member associations threatened to boycott future Fifa competitions.

news.title: Real Madrid backs FIFA’s World Cup stake sale U-turn
news.lede: Real Madrid have backed FIFA‘s decision to withdraw plans to sell a minority stake in the commercial rights of the men’s and women’s World Cups, as pressure mounted on FIFA president Gianni Infantino over the controversial proposal. The 15-time UEFA Champions League winners described the move as “good news for football” after widespread opposition forced FIFA to abandon plans to open its flagship competitions to private investors. Read Also: UEFA threatens FIFA boycott over Infantino’s plan to sell World Cup stake Real Madrid backs FIFA U-turn. Infantino’s proposal had sought to create a new commercial entity through which FIFA would sell minority stakes in the commercial rights of its major tournaments, including the men’s and women’s World Cups.

news.title: Bruno Guimaraes: From Brazil's World Cup villain to the verge of Arsenal's record signing
news.lede: Just weeks after being singled out for Brazil's painful World Cup exit, Bruno Guimaraes is set to become Arsenal's record signing in a reported £80 million move from Newcastle United. The Brazil midfielder, who endured intense criticism after missing a crucial penalty in his country's last-16 defeat to Norway, is expected to sign a five-year contract until 2031, subject to a medical and official confirmation from both clubs. Guimaraes was one of Carlo Ancelotti's standout performers throughout the tournament, but his campaign became defined by one moment. With Brazil level against Norway in the round of 16, the 28-year-old saw his first-half penalty, awarded after a foul on Matheus Cunha, saved by goalkeeper Orjan Nyland.

news.title: FIFA scrap World Cup sell-off plan after backlash
news.lede: This content is provided by Exco Player and may use cookies or similar technologies. Please click 'Allow and Continue' below to load the content. FIFA “will not proceed” with plans to sell stakes in a company which would run the commercial and operational aspects of its competitions, a statement from president Gianni Infantino said. The plan, which would include the men’s and women’s World Cups, has been rejected by three continental confederations with UEFA insisting its nations would boycott FIFA events.

news.title: Chelsea sign Argentina player slapped by Bellingham at World Cup
news.lede: Valentin Barco has agreed a seven-year deal and will link up with Xabi Alonso’s squad during pre-season. Chelsea have announced the signing of Valentín Barco, the Argentina midfielder who was involved in a post-match argument with England’s Jude Bellingham at the World Cup. Last month’s semi-final – like the final – finished in ugly scenes as Bellingham confronted Barco and slapped him on the head, sparking a melee between the two sets of players. The England midfielder appeared to take exception to something Barco had said, having been stood still in a moment of contemplation following the heartbreaking 2-1 defeat before suddenly reacting.
